pages.text: The ground is full of food. It is just very small, and it does not want to be found.$(br2)Get low. Search the soil more than once. Something with a point on it digs better than fingers do.

An empty search tells you why: other primates or Paranthropus working the same ground, a dry day or a dry season, or ground your band has lived off for days - after three it gives less and less. Sometimes it is only bad luck.

Ground gives only so much. Forage one chunk of it successfully a dozen times or so - ten in the dry, eight on a dry day, fifteen in the rains, twenty-five on a $(l)prosperous day$() - and it is picked clean: five days to come back, two in the rains, overnight after a prosperous day.$(br2)$(l)Fertile$() ground gives around fifty and comes back in three days - but nothing marks it. You have to notice it.

$(l)Roots.$() Under a tree, dig with a hand axe or a digging stick: a few strokes and you have roots, which fill you well enough. Live on them, though, and a tooth goes bad - a $(l)dental abscess$(). Draw it out with sweet berries (ten handfuls) or a great deal of water - you can drink past full while it lasts. Leave it two days and it goes into the blood.
Pull at leaves and now and then there are $(l)sweet berries$() in them. Leaves torn off a living tree grow back in a few minutes.$(br2)A $(l)meat chunk$() fills a bar and a half.

Take a $(l)chopper$() to a dead tree and a $(l)dead branch$() comes away - three to a tree. It is no weapon: it breaks on anything it hits. Pick through it for grubs, once; or break it open (sneak) for everything at once, more in hard times. It keeps on a pile with the bones.
